```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "The criterion is a paying customer within 90 days. B shows that merchants already pay for this category: Fairing's tiered pricing ($49–$149/mo), Grapevine's $25/mo plan with 223 reviews, and a cited solo competitor (Zigpoll) at $125K MRR. A shows only published competitor prices. Its competitors include free betas, free open-source tools, waitlist-only offerings and unpriced paid tiers, so the brief has no evidence that anyone in A's niche actually pays yet.",
    "B's distribution channel, the Shopify App Store, is a self-serve marketplace with built-in merchant discovery, so one operator can sell without outbound sales. A's GitHub Marketplace channel needs publisher verification and webhook work, and its free-Action-to-paid conversion is listed as an open question.",
    "A carries trust barriers that slow a first sale. It asks a solo third party for PR-opening access to source code. mendapi's published studies show raw spec diffs over-report by about 8x, which creates false-positive risk. And the higher-paying fintech buyers expect security reviews. B's main trust hurdle, handling customer data, has a known path: a DPA and a privacy review.",
    "B's ceiling is genuinely lower. Six mature competitors offer free tiers, and the poster-child company took two years to gain traction. But this case requires only one paying customer, and in a category where merchants demonstrably pay for this kind of tool, that is a lower bar than proving willingness to pay in a niche with no paid traction shown."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's only acquisition-economics figure, a $248 median devtools CAC with 9.4-month payback, comes from a source page that contained a prompt-injection attempt, and the brief itself says to treat it as directional only. Beyond that, A's whole payer case rests on competitor price lists (apidrift's $29/mo, Nalvis's $14/mo). Neither brief shows that any customer has actually paid those prices.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both briefs describe crowded niches with free incumbents, and neither shows a new entrant winning a paying customer. A's demand evidence is actually stronger: three independent incident quotes versus B's single Reddit quote plus a founder-origin story taken from a seed quote. B wins mainly because its brief shows willingness to pay in the category and has a self-serve marketplace channel. A different reading could reasonably favor A, since its market is newer and less entrenched."
}
```
